sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source represents the outer ridge of the inherited Umbria-Marche thrust system, possibly inverted and re-activated in the current extensional regime.
This NW-SE trending, low-angle, SW-dipping normal fault system is the easternmost one of the central Apennines undergoing extension, just west of the region where compressional activity prevails, in the eastern portion of the central and northern Apennines.
Following the 2016-17 Central Italy seismic sequence, a growing amount of evidence suggests that the large scale thrust systems, originated from the mountain building of the Apennines during the Miocene, are currently experiencing kinematic inversion in the Quaternary extensional regime (Scognamiglio et al., 2018; Bonini et al., 2019; Buttinelli et al., 2021). The active role of inherited thrust systems in the extensional regime has also been confirmed by analog model experiments (Del Ventisette et al., 2021).
This Composite Source straddles the external part of the Umbria-Marche fold and thrust belt. During the Miocene, this fault system controlled the formation of a) the anticlines (e.g., Monte Pietralata and Monte San Vicino anticlines) along the outer ridge of the chain (Barchi et al., 1998; Mazzoli et al., 2002, 2005; Basili and Barba, 2007), and b) the Camerino thrust-top basin to the west.
Historical and instrumental catalogues (ISIDe Working Group, 2007; Guidoboni et al., 2019; Rovida et al., 2021) show a very dense intermediate (4.5 < Mw < 5.0) to damaging seismicity within the area, including the destructive the 28 July 1799 (Mw 6.2) and 12 March 1873 (Mw 5.9) Appennino Marchigiano ones. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenesis in this region, the reader can refer to the respective individual sources in this Database.
